page.title: Modal Perfect and Deduction
page.subtitle_html: Modal Perfect and Deduction - C1 modal perfect forms for past certainty, possibility, regret, and criticism.
page.subtitle_text: C1 modal perfect forms for past certainty, possibility, regret, and criticism.

blocks.body: {"level":"C1","intro":"Modal Perfect and Deduction: compact anchors for using modal + have + V3 in C1 deduction and evaluation.","rules":[{"label":"Past certainty","text":"Use must have + V3 when evidence strongly points to a past conclusion.","example":"He must have forgotten about the meeting."},{"label":"Past possibility","text":"Use may, might, or could have + V3 when several past explanations are possible.","example":"She might have misunderstood the instructions."},{"label":"Regret or criticism","text":"Use should have, ought to have, or needn't have when judging a past action.","example":"They should have checked the figures earlier."}]}

blocks.body: This compact page exists as the theory anchor for the English Sentence Builder C1 modal perfect and deduction lesson package.

page.title: Subjunctive and Formal Structures
page.subtitle_html: Subjunctive and Formal Structures - C1 mandative subjunctive, formal recommendations, and fixed high-register patterns.
page.subtitle_text: C1 mandative subjunctive, formal recommendations, and fixed high-register patterns.

blocks.body: {"level":"C1","intro":"Subjunctive and Formal Structures: compact anchors for formal recommendations, requirements, and fixed high-register patterns.","rules":[{"label":"Mandative subjunctive","text":"After adjectives and verbs of importance, use the base verb in formal English.","example":"It is essential that every applicant submit the form."},{"label":"Formal alternatives","text":"Use should + infinitive or passive structures when the register allows them.","example":"The committee recommended that the policy should be revised."},{"label":"Fixed formal patterns","text":"Use phrases such as lest, be that as it may, and suffice it to say in controlled formal contexts.","example":"The rule was changed lest further confusion arise."}]}

page.title: Subtle Modal Meanings
page.subtitle_html: Subtle Modal Meanings - C2 modal nuance for likelihood, possibility, advice, and necessity.
page.subtitle_text: C2 modal nuance for likelihood, possibility, advice, and necessity.

blocks.body: {"level":"C2","intro":"Subtle modal meanings: compact anchors for nuanced likelihood, tentative advice, theoretical possibility, and unnecessary past action.","rules":[{"label":"Likelihood","text":"Use may well, could well, and might just to express graded possibility.","example":"This may well explain the delay."},{"label":"Soft advice","text":"Use might want to, may be worth, and would be wise to reduce force.","example":"You might want to review the figures again."},{"label":"Past necessity nuance","text":"Contrast need not have with did not need to for past actions and necessity.","example":"They need not have changed the schedule."}]}

blocks.heading: C2 focus
blocks.body: This compact page anchors the English Sentence Builder C2 lesson on subtle modal meanings.
